finding: Scoped materialization planning reserved/released an ancestry frame per visited cell. This created transient ownership bookkeeping and repeatedly consumed fixed stage admission even though sibling visits reuse depth capacity.
fix: Reserve traversal capacity once per maximum depth, merge exclusive reservations without readmission, and release the merged extent when planning ends. No reservation directory or new configuration is added. Null/excluded cells do not acquire frames.

validation.finalAdditionalCase: All six traversal tests and eight materialization-plan tests pass on final merged-reservation implementation.

benchmark.scope: Planning only; borrowed input and subsequent output construction excluded. Prior module uses current dependencies, not a whole historical build. No cloud or total-heap claim.

regressions: Exact fixed-stage planning capacity succeeds across 1000 nested sibling rows; one byte below required depth rejects and cleans up.
Reservation construction is bounded by depth across 1/1000/10000 rows.
Cyclic and invalid nested input errors release all planning charges.
Null/excluded payloads require no depth capacity beyond the traversal base.
remaining: This reduces a demonstrated source of allocation churn; it does not establish whole-runtime caps or solve all metadata accounting.

smallPageComparison.scope: Four alternating fresh-process pairs; only the materialization module is substituted. Not a whole historical build or a universal speedup.

rejectedExperiment.design: The first candidate held each depth via planning.allocate(..., () => undefined). It removed per-cell reservations but added an AtomicMemory owner per depth.
rejectedExperiment.result: One-row-per-page median regressed from 2786.249 to 3032.378 ms. Replaced those owners with the existing exclusive reservation merge contract.

nativeWorkerPressure.boundary: Managed heap still exceeds the 64 MiB admission pool. Sparse single-run heap samples depend on GC timing; no whole-runtime-cap or statistical heap-reduction claim.
